subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and which write paths and default modes are in scope?
rationale: The request adds config surface and changes local filesystem access boundaries across core write paths, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped Policy
options.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with schema/docs/tests and explicit exclusions for sensitive OpenClaw state.

options.title: Use Fixed Defaults Only
options.body: Avoid new config surface and adjust concrete writer defaults only where maintainers approve each boundary, such as user documents or media.

options.title: Document Host Setup
options.body: Leave runtime permissions unchanged and document ACL, Docker user/group, umask, or NAS permission setup as the supported operator path.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with schema/docs/tests and explicit exclusions for sensitive OpenClaw state.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history is on the sandbox and filesystem-safety paths that would need the product/security boundary.
